purpose: Formal pruning and debloat policy for CYNIC crates, modules, and dependency boundaries. Behavior-driven, auditable, revocable.

excludes: isolated experimental fragments unless promoted into the workspace

module_sufficient.description: A module is enough when the boundary is only organizational or narrative, with no independent compilation, reuse, versioning, or test/service reason.
module_sufficient.note: crate splitting is not a goal in itself

conditions: A responsibility changes on a different schedule or reason
A distinct compilation/service requirement (build, runtime, no_std, wasm, isolated test, feature gating, heavy dependency isolation)
A stable public API that is reused, or must be reused
A dependency cycle that forces moving a shared responsibility into a separate crate or shared abstraction

suspect_over_splitting.signal: A crate is too small, too tightly coupled to one consumer, and has no strong reason to live on its own.
suspect_over_splitting.action: Candidate for fusion or return to a module, not yet another crate.

responsibility_rules.clear_owner: Each crate/module must have an identifiable perimeter and a clear contract for what it exposes vs hides.
responsibility_rules.public_surface_contract: Public surface is a commitment; it does not expand without reason.
responsibility_rules.one_way_dependency: Dependency direction must be readable; obscure, implicit, or bidirectional dependencies are avoided without an abstraction.
responsibility_rules.domain_no_infrastructure_by_default: Domain logic must not depend on adapters, infrastructure, framework, driver, or runtime-specific concerns unless it is explicitly that kind of layer.
responsibility_rules.name_states_responsibility: A crate name states ONE responsibility in functional English. It never states a layer (a name may not encode L0-L4, which lives in infra/crate-topology.json and is checked against the real dependency graph), never a vendor or provider prefix used as a category, and never a metaphor. Agave/solana-runtime is the reference: capability names, the layer is declared in Cargo.toml, and the DAG is enforced by the dependency graph rather than by the name.
responsibility_rules.one_responsibility_one_crate: A responsibility has exactly one owning crate. Two crates that both claim it, or that re-export the same surface under a second name, are CONTESTED: the canonical owner wins and the copy is deleted or repointed. Enforced by crates/cynic-host/tests/crate_taxonomy_ownership.rs, which fails when two declared crates share a responsibility or carry an empty one.
responsibility_rules.family_prefix_is_optional_and_not_normat: A family prefix (cynic-host-*, cynic-intel-*, cynic-domain-*) is neither required nor privileged. A crate without a prefix is not in violation; a crate with one does not gain a layer, a purity guarantee, or an exemption. The 'domain' prefix in particular asserts a purity that adapter-bearing crates do not have (cynic-domain-cloudflare and cynic-domain-porkbun both contain adapter.rs and reqwest), so it is retired as a category rather than extended.
responsibility_rules.metaphor_banned_from_crate_names: A metaphor (askesis, kyon, zen) is vocabulary, not a crate name. It may name a concept or a type; it may not name a crate, because a metaphor is what gets used exactly where the responsibility has no functional name, and it then multiplies into collisions (cynic-askesis / cynic-domain-askesis). Renaming a crate that is anchored in a normative contract is a contract change and requires operator admission.
responsibility_rules.llm_comprehensibility: Each crate must be independently comprehensible by an LLM agent with a limited context window. Max 3 external dependencies per crate. Types must be auto-descriptive (no opaque String wrappers). Crate boundaries = agent context boundaries. A crate that cannot be understood in isolation by an LLM agent is a violation.
responsibility_rules.no_std_ready: New types must be no_std-compatible by default. cynic-identity is the model. cynic-protocol must split no_std/std. A new type that requires std without justification is a violation.
responsibility_rules.capability_based_security: Runtime secrets are injected (env, then principal-owned file, then OS store behind a port). Never git, docs, chat logs, or proof JSON. Reports show presence, never the secret. A crate that hardcodes credentials or paths is a violation.

taxonomy.purpose: The executable statement of what a crate IS in this workspace, so the question is answered once rather than re-litigated per agent. Every clause below restates a rule already ratified above or in contracts/foundation.json; none is new. Each names the executor that makes it falsifiable.

crate_is.definition: A crate is one named responsibility, and the unit of compilation, visibility and versioning. It is NOT by itself an architectural boundary: a crate without a minimal `pub` surface and without an architecture test is a directory with a Cargo.toml. The boundary is made by the DAG check, the visibility, and the boundary test together.
crate_is.responsibility: One named responsibility, stated in the crate's Cargo.toml `description`.
crate_is.visibility: `pub` is the only encapsulation Rust provides. A crate whose public surface is broad by convenience has no boundary.
crate_is.versioning: version.workspace = true — one version for the whole workspace.
crate_is.tests: tests/ compiles separately, so it can only exercise the public API.

enforced_by.naming: crates/cynic-host/tests/crate_taxonomy_ownership.rs (empty description, metaphor, layer token, purity prefix)

fcis_and_ddd.policy: The architecture policy in force is Functional Core / Imperative Shell (FCIS) with Data-Oriented Design. CYNIC formally rejects dogmatic Enterprise Java-style Hexagonal Architecture: excessive Arc<dyn Port> indirections destroy CPU cache locality, inhibit compiler inlining, force heap allocations, and multiply boilerplate mock structures. The FCIS solution: (1) Functional Core — 100% pure data structures and deterministic functions, zero async runtimes, zero network sockets, zero mock objects, testable in microseconds; (2) Imperative Shell (adapters/) — direct pragmatic I/O, collects raw kernel data, invokes the pure Functional Core, executes the emitted Action Plan; (3) Zero-Copy and Static Dispatch — parsers parse slices directly without allocating intermediate DTOs. One concept has one home.

verified.core_purity_zero_io: crates/cynic-network/tests/architecture_boundary.rs asserts that I/O primitives (std::process::Command, reqwest, tokio::spawn) appear only under src/adapters/, and that the pure core holds none of them. This is the reference implementation of the FCIS boundary.
verified.dependency_direction: 26 of 48 crates assert no dependency on a higher layer; ARCH-004 checks the whole declared graph against the built one.
verified.concept_ownership: crates/cynic-host/tests/hexagonal_ddd_verifier.rs checks that a domain concept is not defined in two crates. 5 of 6 current collisions are network vocabulary (MeshRegistry, NetworkActuatorActivationPlan, RegistryService) owned by the parallel network session; 1 is CodeCitesProseRule from the audit-engine extraction.

known_gap.statement: The structural half of the policy is NOT verified. Recorded here rather than left implicit, because an unrecorded gap reads as a guarantee.
unverified: that a concept named in two crates has one canonical home (measured 2026-09-30: 10 of 18 sampled concepts have two or more homes; measured 2026-10-06: 5 live collisions, all cynic-network vs cynic-node, 4 of which the parallel network session already repairs)
that an application layer is distinct from the domain and the infrastructure
retired_clauses: that every adapter implements a declared port — RETIRED 2026-10-06. FCIS does not require it: a concrete, trait-unbound adapter is legitimate, and a port with no second implementation is indirection rather than architecture. Port coverage is kept as a MEASUREMENT of indirection, not as a policy requirement.
known_gap.executor: crates/cynic-host/tests/hexagonal_ddd_verifier.rs — concept ownership, plus the generalized FCIS core-purity ratchet (a_pure_core_holds_no_io, measured per crate against FCIS_CORE_IO_BASELINE). Reference implementation of the boundary: crates/cynic-network/tests/architecture_boundary.rs.

known_unknown.layer_of_cynic_host: cynic-host declares L1 and depends on eight L2 domain crates (11 ascending edges). It is declared as tolerated layer debt in infra/crate-topology.json. Whether it is an L1 substrate crate or an L2 composition crate is not decided by this contract; the ascending edges are the evidence that the current label is wrong.
known_unknown.responsibility_bound: CRATE_RULES.md §5 leaves the 'responsibilities <= N' threshold to the operator. Not decided here.

visibility_rules.tightest_usable: Use the narrowest visibility that communicates intent. Private by default, pub(crate) for internal shared detail, pub only where it is a real public API.
visibility_rules.no_permanent_broadening: Do not keep a module or item permanently over-opened for a temporary convenience. If opened, document why and close it again when possible.

pruning_rules.remove_orphans_first: Orphaned, abandoned, or non-verified modules/crates with no real reason are removal or fusion candidates, before structural design.
pruning_rules.no_footprint_justification: Do not keep code 'just in case' without a current reason. A pure future justification without a present trigger is archived or isolated, not kept as passive debt.
pruning_rules.extract_only_with_real_reason: Before extracting a crate, verify the reason for the crate is real and current. A hypothetical future reason is delayed or documented with a trigger, not used to force a new crate now.
pruning_rules.no_split_for_split_sake: Do not fragment into more crates to satisfy an empty formal rule.

debt_and_cleanup_rules.debt_as_state: Treat debt as a measurable, owned state, not vague discomfort. 'Old' is not enough by itself.
debt_and_cleanup_rules.deduplication_before_new_abstraction: Merge proven duplication before introducing new abstractions.
debt_and_cleanup_rules.refactor_for_reason: Refactor from an identified problem, with a proposed fix, verified effects, and only the necessary moves.

maintenance_rules.verify_before_touching: Verify users, dependencies, tests, references, build effects, and runtime impact before touching a module or crate.
maintenance_rules.no_refactor_by_default: Refactor from a real identified problem, not from a desire to move code for its own sake.

violations.god_module: One module or crate accumulating unrelated responsibilities with no clear boundary is a violation signal, not yet a verdict.
violations.dumping_ground: A module that becomes a catch-all without a coherent responsibility is a violation signal.
violations.framework_in_domain: Domain code importing framework, driver, runtime, or infrastructure-specific types without an explicit adapter role is a violation signal.
violations.broad_pub_by_convenience: Permanent over-broad visibility used to avoid a real boundary is a violation signal.
violations.name_encodes_layer_or_vendor: A crate name that asserts a layer, a purity, or a vendor as its category. The DAG is machine readable in infra/crate-topology.json and in the Cargo graph; duplicating it in a name creates collisions the graph cannot see.
violations.responsibility_has_two_owners: Two crates declaring or implementing the same responsibility. This is the defect that produced five homes for Claim, Scope and Budget; it is now a gate, not a comment.

known_ambiguities.suspect_to_small_crate_threshold: The exact threshold for 'too small a crate' is contextual; the rule gives a signal, not an automatic verdict.
known_ambiguities.module_vs_crate_elasticity: The line can shift over time when a reason becomes real or disappears.

known_exclusions: This policy does not replace verification of code, tests, dependencies, build, and real impact.
This policy does not decide automatically; it produces signals and decision rules.

ratification.why: This policy was used as the decision rule for the whole crate fusion programme — contracts/crate-fusion-dispositions.json applies crate_justified and suspect_over_splitting to 10 candidates, and those dispositions are only proposals rather than opinions because the rule they were derived from is now authority. A contract left in draft while being used to rule is the same failure as a denylist nobody compares: it looks like a policy and decides nothing.
ratification.applies_to_the_agent: This policy is the authority for whether a crate may be created, fused, or removed. It is machine-checked in part by ARCH-004 in cynic-host::audit_engine, which enforces the justification clause against the observed manifests, and the remainder is carried by contracts/crate-fusion-dispositions.json, whose lists may only shrink.
ratification.amendment_2026_09_29: Added name_states_responsibility, one_responsibility_one_crate, family_prefix_is_optional_and_not_normative and metaphor_banned_from_crate_names, plus two entries under violations. Ratified by the operator on 2026-09-29 after re-studying the Agave model. Basis: Agave keeps a single Cargo workspace with root-level shared lints, names crates by capability, puts the layer in Cargo.toml rather than in the name, and gates unstable surfaces behind a feature flag. Its own counter-example is documented in this amendment: the solana-* to agave-* rename broke automations, which is what happens when a prefix encodes provenance rather than responsibility. Enforcement: crates/cynic-host/tests/crate_taxonomy_ownership.rs.
